item.title: CVE-2026-133620 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.3
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 5.3 | Flowintel's template repository subsystem did not adequately constrain file access to the configured repository base directory. Two related weaknesses existed:
- Repository registration and editing accepted arbitrary local paths without verifying they resolved inside the configured REPOSITORY_BASE_PATH, allowing an authenticated user to point a repository at any readable directory on the host. - Manifest and template file lookups used normalized (non-canonical) path joins and a startswith-based guard that could be bypassed by symbolic links, permitting reads of files outside the intended repository.
An authenticated user with the ability to add or edit a template repository could therefore cause the application to read and return the contents of arbitrary files readable by the service account, including configuration files, credentials, or other sensitive data.
Affected: Flowintel versions prior to 4.1.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-133622 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 3.7
item.description: Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 3.7 | A flaw was found in certmonger. Certmonger fails to enforce size limits or transfer timeouts when downloading and buffering Simple Certificate Enrollment Protocol (SCEP) replies over HTTP. item.title: CVE-2026-133626 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 7.1
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 7.1 | FlowIntel contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in its file-to-note conversion feature. When a user converts an attached CSV or JSON file into a case note, the application renders the data as a Markdown table by padding every row to the maximum column count. A crafted file with a small number of filled cells but a very large number of columns (or keys) causes the application to allocate a quadratic number of padded table cells, potentially exhausting a worker process in memory or CPU.
The same issue affects nested JSON values rendered inside table cells, where pretty-printed indentation further inflates the output size.
Preconditions: - An authenticated user with access to a case in FlowIntel - Ability to attach and convert a CSV or JSON file to a note
Impact: - Denial of service: exhaustion of a worker process, potentially disrupting service for other users - No confidentiality or integrity impact
Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0

item.title: CVE-2026-133627 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.3
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 5.3 | flowintel contains a log injection vulnerability in its case history (audit log) subsystem. The case history is stored as a line-delimited file where each line represents a single event attributed to a specific user. User-controlled fields, including user names, event messages, and case titles used during case merging, were written to the history file without sanitizing embedded line separator characters (such as carriage return, line feed, vertical tab, form feed, and Unicode line/paragraph separators).
An authenticated user with the ability to create or modify case history entries could embed line separators in these fields. Upon writing, the injected separators would split a single intended entry into multiple lines, each of which the history format interprets as a distinct event. This allows an attacker to forge additional history entries attributed to arbitrary users, corrupting the audit trail and undermining the integrity of case records.
The vulnerability affects the case history append and merge operations. No authentication bypass or privilege escalation is required beyond normal case-management access.
Affected versions: flowintel prior to 4.1.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-115409 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5 | In `github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11/v2` versions `<= 2.0.0-rc8` (and the deprecated v1 module paths `github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11 <= 1.6.8`, `github.com/ThalesGroup/crypto11 <= 1.7.0-rc1` and `github.com/ThalesIgnite/crypto11 <= 1.2.5`), the key-pair and certificate lookup functions (`FindKeyPair`, `FindKeyPairs`, `FindKeyPairsWithAttributes`, `FindAllKeyPairs`, the `FindRSAKeyPair*` family and `FindAllPairedCertificates`) pair a private key with a public key object, or with a certificate, by `CKA_ID`/`CKA_LABEL` alone, take the first match the token returns, and never verify that it belongs to the private key. PKCS#11 permits a session that has not logged in to create public token objects, so anyone able to open a session on the token — without the PIN — can plant a public key or certificate carrying a victim key's `CKA_ID` and label, and crypto11 may return it as that key's public half. An application that publishes or trusts `Signer.Public()` (a JWKS endpoint, a key registry, `authorized_keys`, a CSR) then publishes the attacker's key, and relying parties accept anything the attacker signs as coming from the service. On the v1 line the lookup also falls back to a class-and-key-type-only search when the private key has no `CKA_ID`, pairing a label-only private key with the first public key of its type on the token.
The v1 module paths are deprecated and will not be fixed; users should migrate to github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11/v2 version 2.0.0-rc9 or later.

item.title: CVE-2026-121790 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.2
item.description: Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.2 | The CWILL (Formerly ParcelPanel) – Shipment Tracking, Tracking & Order Tracking for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data[].courier_code, data[].tracking_number (plus pp_sign for the auth bypass)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.6.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. item.title: CVE-2026-125085 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8
item.description: Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.8 | The Nexter Extension – Security, Performance, Code Snippets & Site Toolkit plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in versions up to, and including, 4.9.0 This is due to the role_switcher_to_view_admin_as() function handling the `reset-view` branch without a capability check or nonce when the caller's own login is supplied, combined with an incomplete cleanup hook (maybe_prevent_switchback_to_administrator) that exits early when the user's current roles equal the stored view role and that is never triggered when WordPress core's WP_User::set_role() short-circuits because the account already has only the target role. item.title: CVE-2026-126716 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.1
item.description: Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.1 | The Mega Forms – Drag & Drop Form Builder with Multi-Step & Conditional Logic plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the delete_entry function in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.9 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). item.title: CVE-2026-133630 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 5.9
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 5.9 | The flowintel Docker build workflow used the GitHub Actions checkout action with default credential persistence, causing the job authentication token to be written into the repository's Git configuration file. This file became part of the Docker build context and could be retained in exported build cache layers, even though Git metadata was stripped from the final runtime image.
An attacker with access to the CI/CD build cache or build environment could extract the persisted token and use it to gain unauthorized access to the private source repository.

item.title: CVE-2026-133631 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 7.1
item.description:
Friday 20 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 7.1 | FlowIntel contains multiple security flaws in its note variable resolution, chatbot API tooling, and AI report generation.
- Note variable references (e.g. cross-case or cross-task lookups) were resolved using the viewing user's privileges rather than the destination case's audience. An authenticated user with access to a shared or imported note could embed references to private cases, causing sensitive case data to be pulled into AI report requests, exports, and MISP sends without the referenced case's audience having granted read access.
- The chatbot API tool permitted the language model to invoke any FlowIntel API endpoint, including administrative routes and state-changing GET operations, without an allow-list or path validation. An attacker who can influence the model's instructions (e.g. via untrusted case content) could induce data modification or access restricted endpoints.
- AI report generation passed the Ollama bearer token and full case content as command-line arguments to a child process, exposing them in the system process table to any local user.
Affected versions: FlowIntel prior to 4.1.0.
